status_as_of_cutoff: Site work-construction. Amazon announced a ceremonial groundbreaking on October 30, 2025, and local reporting from the Richmond County commissioners context reported site clearing, grubbing, excavation/grading preparations, and roughly 250 acres cleared by late October 2025. NC DEQ's July 2026 materials still describe Amazon.25A and DukeRichmond.26C as draft/preliminary air permit actions with comments accepted through July 31, 2026; no final air permit decision, building permit, CO, grid connection, or energized IT load was verified as of the 2026-08-11 refresh.
evidence_grade: B - official state/company sources confirm announcement, address, air-permit process, 21-building plan, and groundbreaking; local reporting supports active site clearing/grading; final permits/energization remain unverified.

actions.government_body: North Carolina Department of Commerce / Governor
actions.result_status: State announced Amazon's planned $10 billion North Carolina investment and Richmond County partnership. Announcement is not a building permit or proof of construction.
actions.access_caveat: State economic-development announcement; underlying county incentive agreement and local permit files were not located.
actions.evidence_note: State/company announcement kept separate from land-use/building approval.

actions.government_body: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Air Quality
actions.action_type: air / draft Title V permit and public notice
actions.result_status: DEQ announced draft permits for Amazon's Energy Way Tech Campus and Duke Energy bridge-power facility, including 588 Amazon emergency engines and 57 Duke engines. The action was preliminary and subject to hearing/comment; it was not final approval.
actions.access_caveat: Draft air permits concern generators/power and do not establish building occupancy, grid interconnection, or energized IT load.

actions.government_body: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality / Richmond County public hearing
actions.action_type: air / scheduled public hearing after cutoff
actions.result_status: DEQ scheduled a public hearing on the preliminary determination for Amazon and Duke air applications for July 30, 2026, after the July 16 cutoff. No final permit decision was available at cutoff.
actions.access_caveat: Future scheduled event recorded as pending; it is not treated as a completed hearing or approval.

actions.government_body: Amazon Web Services / Richmond County event
actions.result_status: Amazon reported a groundbreaking celebration for the Richmond County data center campus. Local reporting one day later said Amazon had begun clearing land at Energy Way Industrial Park and that construction was already underway at the 700-acre industrial site, with about 250 acres cleared.
actions.access_caveat: Groundbreaking is company-reported and partly ceremonial; active clearing/grading detail is supported by local reporting, not a county permit file.
actions.evidence_note: Supports status upgrade from announced/local process to site work-construction, but not energization.

actions.result_status: Amazon stated the Richmond County campus will include 21 buildings and that it had applied to NC DAQ for an air quality permit for backup generators at the campus.
actions.access_caveat: Company explanation; the permit decision remains with NC DEQ/DAQ.
actions.evidence_note: Confirms current owner/operator narrative and building count; not capacity MW.

actions.government_body: North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Air Quality
actions.result_status: DEQ's notice kept Amazon.25A and DukeRichmond.26C in preliminary/draft status and accepted comments through July 31, 2026. Current search did not locate a final air permit issuance.
actions.access_caveat: Absence of a located final decision is not proof that none will issue later; refresh should re-check DEQ Laserfiche/press releases.
actions.evidence_note: Pending air action only; no final air approval verified.

capacity_note: No reliable MW capacity was found in official or local-government sources. Current official/company facts describe a planned $10 billion, 21-building campus, 588 Amazon emergency engines, and 57 Duke bridge-power engines, but not IT load MW.

contradictions.topic: Air-permit source aggregation and generator counts
contradictions.description: Official DEQ/company material treats Amazon backup generation and Duke bridge-power generation as separate applications and describes 588 Amazon emergency engines plus 57 Duke bridge-power engines. SELC/NCSU-linked commentary argues the generators should be treated as a single source and cites different aggregate counts in some materials. The refresh keeps the official DEQ counts as primary and records the dispute as unresolved pending final DEQ action.
